value.body: Company secretaries handle corporate governance and compliance: board and shareholder meetings, statutory filings, securities-law compliance and corporate restructuring. Inside companies they work in secretarial, legal or compliance teams; in practice they run secretarial audits and advisory work. The role is created by law for many companies, which keeps demand steady.

items.label: Who must appoint a whole-time CS
items.value: Listed companies and companies with paid-up capital of ₹10 crore or more
items.note: Companies Act 2013, s.203 with Rules 8 and 8A

items.label: Secretarial audit
items.note: Required for listed and certain large companies — Companies Act 2013, s.204

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Membership of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) after clearing the CS Executive and Professional exams and practical training. Companies hire members directly; practising CSs need a certificate of practice from ICSI.

value.title: At a glance
items: Typical in-house roles: company secretary, compliance officer, legal and secretarial executive.
Listed and regulated companies (banks, NBFCs, insurers) offer the most structured compliance roles.
An LLB alongside CS widens legal-team options.
Practice income depends on building a client base.
